name: Git and GitHub
desc: เก็บประวัติโค้ด ทำงานร่วมกันเป็นทีม และใช้โชว์ Portfolio
pre: 19 Linux (basics). Day 0 already set git config and made the first commit in ~/projects/learning-journal. In the recommended order the learner has already finished: 19 Linux
why: เริ่มเก็บงานทุกชิ้นลง GitHub ตั้งแต่ต้น เมื่อเรียนจบจะมี Portfolio สะสมไว้แล้ว
core: Backend, Full-stack JS, AI Engineer, Data Scientist, Cyber Security, Network, Android, Game Dev, Product Builder
proj: Portfolio Website บน GitHub Pages

A personal portfolio site (static HTML/CSS) in its own repository, developed with feature branches and pull requests, a GitHub Actions workflow that validates HTML/links on every PR, deployed with GitHub Pages, with a profile README; also push the learning-journal repo from Day 0
Git Flow, CI/CD เบื้องต้น
guide: Git 2.43 on Ubuntu 24.04. Cover: what version control is and why; repository, working tree, staging area, commits (with a clear diagram in text); git init/status/add/commit/log/diff/show; writing good commit messages (Conventional Commits); .gitignore; undoing safely (git restore, git restore --staged, git commit --amend, git revert, git reset --soft/--mixed/--hard with clear warnings, git reflog to recover); branches (git switch -c, merge, fast-forward vs merge commit); resolving merge conflicts step by step; rebase (and the golden rule of not rebasing shared history); stash; tags and releases; remotes: creating an SSH key (ssh-keygen -t ed25519), adding it to GitHub, testing with ssh -T git@github.com, git remote add, push -u, fetch, pull (merge vs rebase), clone; forks and pull requests, code review etiquette, GitHub Issues and Projects; GitHub CLI gh (installation per GitHub's official instructions for Ubuntu; gh auth login, gh pr create); GitHub Actions (workflow YAML syntax, triggers, jobs, a test workflow); GitHub Pages deployment; branching strategies (GitHub flow, trunk-based); git bisect, cherry-pick, blame; protecting secrets (.env in .gitignore, what to do if a secret was pushed, GitHub secret scanning); Git LFS overview; licenses and the profile README. In the sandbox you cannot reach github.com: simulate remotes with a local bare repository (git init --bare) so push/pull/fetch/conflict examples produce REAL output, and write GitHub-only steps carefully, saying what the learner will see. Certifications: GitHub Foundations GH-900 (plus GH-200 Actions, GH-300 Copilot, GH-500 Advanced Security, GH-100 Administration).

name: Python
desc: ภาษาที่อ่านง่ายที่สุด ใช้ได้ทั้ง Automation, Web, Data, AI และ Security
pre: 19 Linux (Terminal basics) and 17 Git and GitHub. In the recommended order the learner has already finished: 19 Linux, 17 Git and GitHub
why: Syntax อ่านง่ายที่สุด เหมาะเป็นภาษาแรก และใช้ได้เกือบทุกสาย
core: Backend, AI Engineer, Data Scientist, Cyber Security
should: Network, Android, Game Dev, Product Builder
proj: argparse CLI that adds/lists/edits/deletes expenses with categories and dates, stores data in CSV and exports JSON, shows monthly summaries per category, validates input, has a pytest test suite and ruff formatting, and is packaged with a requirements file
guide: This is the learner's FIRST programming language: explain programming ideas from zero (what a program/variable/function is) with very gentle pacing at the beginner level, then go deep. Use the system python3 3.12 on Ubuntu 24.04 for scripts and a venv (python3 -m venv .venv; source .venv/bin/activate) for packages; explain the externally-managed-environment error. Cover: running scripts and the REPL; variables and basic types; strings and f-strings; numbers and math; input/output; conditionals; loops (for/while, range, break/continue); lists, tuples, sets, dicts; comprehensions; functions (parameters, defaults, *args/**kwargs, return, type hints, docstrings); modules and packages, the if __name__ == '__main__' idiom; files with pathlib/open, csv and json modules; exceptions (try/except/else/finally, raising, custom exceptions); OOP (classes, methods, inheritance, dataclasses); iterators and generators; decorators; context managers; standard library tour (datetime, collections, itertools, argparse, logging, random); virtual environments, pip and requirements.txt with pinned versions; testing with pytest; formatting and linting with ruff; debugging (print debugging, breakpoint()/pdb, VS Code debugger); basic data structures and algorithms (big-O intuition, searching, sorting, dict vs list lookup timing with timeit); calling HTTP APIs with requests or httpx (test against a local http.server or a small local JSON endpoint because the sandbox blocks most internet). Run every example with python3 in the sandbox and paste real output (the sandbox is 3.13 — do not use 3.13-only features; target 3.12). Certifications: PCEP-30-02 (PCEP-30-03 due 2026-10-31), PCAP-31-03 (PCAP-31-04 due 2026-10-31).

name: Prompt Engineering
desc: เทคนิคสื่อสารกับ AI ให้ได้ผลแม่นยำ สม่ำเสมอ และวัดผลได้
pre: nothing strictly required (recommended: 9 Python, for the code-based concepts). In the recommended order the learner has already finished: 19 Linux, 17 Git and GitHub, 9 Python
why: เมื่อเขียนโค้ดเป็นแล้ว ก็ใช้ AI เป็นติวเตอร์และทดสอบ Prompt ด้วยโค้ดได้
should: Backend, Full-stack JS, Data Scientist, Cyber Security, Network, Android, Game Dev
proj: A git-versioned library of prompt templates (YAML) plus a Python evaluation harness that runs each prompt against test cases with checks (keyword, regex, JSON schema, length, LLM-as-judge), works in mock mode without an API key and in real mode with Claude, and prints a comparison report between prompt versions
guide: The learner knows Linux, Git and basic Python at this point. Cover: what an LLM is (tokens, next-token prediction, context window, why it hallucinates, why outputs vary); the anatomy of a good prompt (role/system, task, context, constraints, output format, examples); clarity and specificity (show bad vs improved prompts side by side with the mock outputs that illustrate the difference); giving context, audience and success criteria; few-shot examples; letting the model reason (explain that current models think internally and that effort controls depth, rather than old 'think step by step' tricks); structured output (JSON with schemas, XML tags to separate instructions from data); prompt chaining and task decomposition; role prompting; handling long documents (documents first, ask for quotes, ground answers); reducing hallucinations (allow 'I don't know', require citations to provided text); prompt templates with variables in Python; evaluating prompts (test cases, rubrics, automated checks, LLM-as-judge) and iterating with version control; prompt injection and safety; Thai-language prompting tips (state the output language, mixing Thai and English terms, tokenization cost of Thai text measured with count_tokens in real mode); using AI as a tutor responsibly (link to Master Roadmap study system); cost, tokens and caching basics. Every concept must include a runnable Python harness example (mock mode prints realistic, fixed outputs) plus the prompt itself in a tpl block. Read /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/fe474bf2-4538-5703-885b-2ffd0c503494/scratchpad/spec/AI_GUIDE.md before writing any LLM code: it has the current SDK usage, exact model IDs, parameters that now return errors, and the mandatory no-key mock mode. Certifications: none mainstream; mention free vendor courses and docs instead.

name: SQL
desc: ภาษาสำหรับจัดการและวิเคราะห์ข้อมูลในฐานข้อมูลเชิงสัมพันธ์
pre: nothing strictly required (recommended: 19 Linux, 9 Python for the Python-integration concepts). In the recommended order the learner has already finished: 19 Linux, 17 Git and GitHub, 9 Python, 16 Prompt Engineering
why: ข้อมูลคือหัวใจของทุกระบบ และใช้ Python เชื่อมต่อกับ Database ได้ทันที
should: AI Engineer, Cyber Security, Android, Product Builder
proj: Design and build an e-commerce database (customers, categories, products, orders, order_items, payments) in PostgreSQL 16 with constraints and indexes, a deterministic seed script, an ER diagram in text, 20 analytical queries (with real outputs) answering business questions, EXPLAIN-based index tuning, and a Python report script using parameterized queries
guide: Start with SQLite 3.45 (sudo apt install sqlite3; .mode box/.headers on) for zero-setup practice, then move to PostgreSQL 16 (sudo apt install postgresql; sudo service postgresql start; sudo -u postgres psql; createuser/createdb for the learner). Show where SQLite and PostgreSQL syntax differ (dates, string functions, autoincrement vs identity, boolean). Use one consistent sample schema throughout (e.g. a small shop) with seed data provided in full. Cover: what a relational database is; tables, rows, columns, keys; data types; CREATE TABLE with constraints (PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, CHECK, DEFAULT); INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE; WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT/OFFSET, DISTINCT, LIKE/ILIKE, IN, BETWEEN; NULL semantics and COALESCE; aggregates with GROUP BY and HAVING; JOINs (INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL, self, cross) with diagrams in text; subqueries (scalar, IN, EXISTS, correlated); CTEs and recursive CTEs; window functions (ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, SUM/AVG OVER, LAG/LEAD, running totals); CASE; set operations; string and date functions; views; indexes and EXPLAIN / EXPLAIN ANALYZE (and EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN in SQLite); normalization (1NF–3NF) and denormalization trade-offs; transactions, ACID, isolation levels with a two-session demo; roles and GRANT; backup and restore (pg_dump/psql); using SQL from Python (sqlite3 and psycopg 3 with parameterized queries; why string formatting causes SQL injection). Run EVERY query in the sandbox and paste the real result tables. Certifications: no single SQL certification is required; vendor certifications (Oracle, Microsoft, PostgreSQL vendors) exist — tell learners to verify current names and exam codes.

name: Network Engineer
desc: เข้าใจว่าข้อมูลเดินทางในเครือข่ายอย่างไร (OSI, TCP/IP, IP, DNS, Routing) และดูแลเครือข่ายองค์กร
pre: 19 Linux. In the recommended order the learner has already finished: 19 Linux, 17 Git and GitHub, 9 Python, 16 Prompt Engineering, 14 SQL
why: ต้องเข้าใจ IP, DNS, HTTP ก่อนสร้างเว็บหรือ API
proj: Python toolkit: subnet calculator (ipaddress), DNS lookup, port check against the learner's own machine only, a text network report, plus a home network diagram
guide: Cover from zero to job-ready: OSI and TCP/IP models; Ethernet, MAC, ARP; IPv4 addressing, subnetting and CIDR (many worked examples); IPv6 basics; DHCP; DNS (record types, resolution, dig/nslookup); TCP vs UDP, ports, 3-way handshake; HTTP/HTTPS/TLS basics; NAT/PAT; routing (routing table, default gateway, static routes; OSPF and BGP concepts); switching (VLANs, 802.1Q trunking, STP basics); Wi-Fi basics; firewalls and ACLs; VPN concepts; a troubleshooting methodology. Tools on Ubuntu (WSL): ip, ping, tracepath/traceroute, mtr, ss, dig, curl -v, tcpdump (on lo or own traffic), nmap ONLY against 127.0.0.1/own containers. Windows tools: ipconfig /all, Test-NetConnection, tracert, nslookup, Get-NetIPAddress. Wireshark runs on Windows. WSL2 networking: default NAT mode gives the distro its own virtual IP; Windows 11 supports networkingMode=mirrored in %UserProfile%\.wslconfig (verify wording, explain trade-offs). Device configuration labs: Cisco Packet Tracer (free with a Cisco Networking Academy account) or GNS3/Containerlab; show Cisco IOS command examples (enable, configure terminal, interface config, ip address, vlan, switchport mode access/trunk, ip route, router ospf, show ip interface brief, show running-config) in plaintext blocks with data-env app and label 'Cisco IOS · Packet Tracer' — these cannot be run in the sandbox, so follow official IOS syntax carefully. Python network automation: socket, ipaddress, subprocess; mention Netmiko/NAPALM/Ansible as next steps (concept only unless tested). Certifications: CompTIA Network+ N10-009, Cisco CCNA 200-301 (v1.1 until 2027-02-02, v2.0 from 2027-02-03), CCNP Enterprise. Safety: only scan/test devices you own.

name: JavaScript
desc: ภาษาของเว็บเบราว์เซอร์ ใช้ทำหน้าเว็บแบบ Interactive และใช้ทำ Server ผ่าน Node.js ได้ด้วย
pre: 17 Git and GitHub (recommended: 9 Python already learned, so this is the second language). In the recommended order the learner has already finished: 19 Linux, 17 Git and GitHub, 9 Python, 16 Prompt Engineering, 14 SQL, 1 Network Engineer
why: ภาษาเดียวที่รันในเบราว์เซอร์ได้ เป็นภาษาที่สองที่ดี เพราะตอนนี้เข้าใจหลักการเขียนโปรแกรมจาก Python แล้ว
proj: Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript quiz app in the browser: questions loaded with fetch from a local JSON file, DOM rendering, events, timer, score, localStorage high score, accessible UI, served locally (python3 -m http.server), with node:test unit tests for the pure logic module
guide: This topic must ALSO teach the HTML and CSS basics needed to work with the DOM (structure, semantic tags, forms, selectors, box model, flexbox), because no other topic covers them. Install Node.js LTS via nvm v0.40.8 for running JS outside the browser. Cover: running JS (browser DevTools console, <script type=module>, node file.js); variables (let/const), types, operators, equality (=== vs ==); strings and template literals; conditionals and loops; functions, arrow functions, default/rest params; arrays and methods (map, filter, reduce, find, some, sort pitfalls); objects, destructuring, spread, optional chaining, nullish coalescing; ES modules (import/export); scope, closures, hoisting, 'this'; classes; error handling (try/catch, Error types); DOM selection and manipulation; events and event delegation; forms and validation; localStorage/JSON; async JS: callbacks, promises, async/await, fetch and JSON, the event loop (microtasks vs macrotasks with a demo); debugging with DevTools; npm basics; testing with node:test (built in). Browser examples must still be verifiable: run them in the sandbox headless with Playwright (Chromium is preinstalled at /opt/pw-browsers; global node module 'playwright' 1.56 is available via NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g)) or jsdom, and paste the real console output. Use data-env app with label 'JavaScript · Browser Console' or file blocks like 'HTML · index.html'. Certifications: no certification the market relies on; portfolio matters most.

name: TypeScript
desc: JavaScript ที่เพิ่มระบบ Type ช่วยจับ Bug ก่อนรัน นิยมมากในงานจริง
pre: 4 JavaScript. In the recommended order the learner has already finished: 19 Linux, 17 Git and GitHub, 9 Python, 16 Prompt Engineering, 14 SQL, 1 Network Engineer, 4 JavaScript
why: ต่อยอดจาก JS ทันทีตอนที่ยังจำ JS ได้ดี
proj: TypeScript CLI task manager with typed domain models, discriminated unions for commands, generics for a repository layer, zod validation at the JSON-file boundary, strict tsconfig, compiled with tsc 7 and tested with node:test
guide: Use TypeScript 7.x (latest 7.0.2, the Go-native compiler; command still `tsc`): npm install -D typescript@7 in a project folder. The sandbox has a global tsc 6.0.2 — always test with a local TypeScript 7 install (npm is reachable) and use a modern strict tsconfig that TS 7 accepts (check for removed/deprecated options; e.g. use module nodenext/esnext and a modern target; do not use options TS 7 rejects). Mention that some tools that use the TypeScript API may still require 6.x. Also show Node's built-in type stripping (running .ts files directly with node for erasable syntax only) — verify the exact behaviour on Node 22 in the sandbox and state which Node versions support it unflagged. Cover: why TypeScript; setup and tsconfig (strict); primitive types and inference; arrays and tuples; object types, interfaces vs type aliases; optional and readonly; union and intersection types; literal types; narrowing (typeof, in, instanceof, discriminated unions, exhaustive checks with never); functions (parameter/return types, overloads); classes and access modifiers; generics and constraints; utility types (Partial, Required, Pick, Omit, Record, ReturnType, Awaited); keyof, typeof, indexed access; mapped and conditional types; template literal types; enums vs union literals (prefer unions; erasableSyntaxOnly); modules and declaration files (.d.ts, @types packages); any vs unknown vs never; typing async code and fetch; runtime validation with zod at boundaries; TypeScript with Node and the DOM; testing; migrating a JS project to TS step by step. Run every example (tsc output errors included) in the sandbox and paste real compiler output.

name: Node.js
desc: รัน JavaScript นอกเบราว์เซอร์ เพื่อสร้าง Server, CLI และ API
pre: 4 JavaScript (recommended: 15 TypeScript). In the recommended order the learner has already finished: 19 Linux, 17 Git and GitHub, 9 Python, 16 Prompt Engineering, 14 SQL, 1 Network Engineer, 4 JavaScript, 15 TypeScript
why: ใช้ JS/TS สร้าง Server ได้ เป็นสะพานไปสู่ Backend
proj: Express 5 REST service that creates short codes for URLs, redirects with 301/302, counts clicks, validates input with zod, stores data in SQLite (better-sqlite3), has rate limiting and helmet, structured logging with pino, node:test + supertest tests, and environment config via --env-file
guide: Install Node.js LTS via nvm v0.40.8 (nvm install --lts). The sandbox has Node 22 — write code that runs on Node 24 and 26 and avoid anything that does not exist in 22. Use ES modules ("type": "module"). Cover: what Node is (V8, libuv, event loop, non-blocking I/O, when Node fits); REPL and running scripts; ESM vs CommonJS; npm, package.json, scripts, semver, package-lock.json, npx; core modules (fs/promises, path, os, events/EventEmitter, stream, http, url, crypto); process, argv, environment variables and node --env-file; async patterns and error handling (unhandled rejections); a raw HTTP server with node:http; Express 5 (routing, middleware, error-handling middleware, async errors in Express 5); building a REST API with validation (zod); persistence with SQLite via better-sqlite3 (or a JSON file for the very first step); testing with node:test and supertest; debugging (node --inspect, VS Code); security (helmet, express-rate-limit, input validation, npm audit); logging with pino; streams and backpressure; worker_threads overview; production concerns (process managers like pm2 or systemd, graceful shutdown, Docker image basics). Pin and test every npm package version in the sandbox (npm is reachable). Certifications: none the market relies on; mention that OpenJS certification availability changes and must be checked.

name: API Design
desc: ออกแบบ "สัญญา" ให้โปรแกรมคุยกัน: REST, HTTP, JSON, OpenAPI, Auth, Versioning
pre: 1 Network Engineer (HTTP basics), and one server-side language: 9 Python or 13 Node.js. In the recommended order the learner has already finished: 19 Linux, 17 Git and GitHub, 9 Python, 16 Prompt Engineering, 14 SQL, 1 Network Engineer, 4 JavaScript, 15 TypeScript, 13 Node.js
why: รู้ทั้ง HTTP และภาษาฝั่ง Server แล้ว พร้อมออกแบบ API อย่างเป็นระบบ
should: Data Scientist, Cyber Security, Android, Product Builder
proj: Contract-first design of a library (books, members, loans) REST API: an OpenAPI 3.1 YAML spec with schemas, examples, errors (RFC 9457 problem details), pagination and auth; linted with Spectral, mocked with Prism, plus a small FastAPI reference implementation and curl test script
guide: Cover: what an API is and API styles; HTTP methods, safety and idempotency, status codes (with when to use each), headers; REST principles (resources, nouns, statelessness, HATEOAS mentioned briefly); URL and resource naming; query parameters, filtering, sorting, pagination (offset vs cursor); JSON request/response design and naming conventions; error format with RFC 9457 Problem Details (application/problem+json); versioning strategies; idempotency keys for POST; authentication (API keys, OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect concepts, JWT structure and pitfalls) and authorization; rate limiting (429 + Retry-After); caching (ETag/If-None-Match, Cache-Control); CORS; OpenAPI 3.1 in YAML (paths, components/schemas, examples, securitySchemes); contract-first workflow; mock servers with Prism (npx @stoplight/prism-cli) and linting with Spectral (npx @stoplight/spectral-cli) — test both in the sandbox (npm is reachable) and pin versions; API documentation (Swagger UI / Redoc); testing APIs with curl and pytest; implementing a reference API with FastAPI (pin versions) to demonstrate status codes and validation; webhooks; GraphQL and gRPC compared with REST; OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023). Run every curl example against a local server in the sandbox and paste real output (including headers with curl -i where useful).

name: Backend
desc: สร้างระบบหลังบ้าน: Server, Database, Auth, Cache, Testing, Deployment
pre: 9 Python (or 13 Node.js), 14 SQL, 8 API Design, 1 Network Engineer, 17 Git and GitHub. In the recommended order the learner has already finished: 19 Linux, 17 Git and GitHub, 9 Python, 16 Prompt Engineering, 14 SQL, 1 Network Engineer, 4 JavaScript, 15 TypeScript, 13 Node.js, 8 API Design
why: รวม SQL + API + Network + ภาษา เป็นระบบจริงที่ Deploy ได้
should: AI Engineer, Cyber Security, Android, Product Builder
proj: A task-management REST API in FastAPI with users, password hashing, JWT auth, role-based authorization, PostgreSQL 16 via SQLAlchemy 2 + Alembic migrations (SQLite for tests), pagination, validation, structured logging, health check, Redis caching for one endpoint, pytest test suite, Dockerfile + docker compose, and a GitHub Actions CI workflow
guide: Primary stack: Python + FastAPI (pin versions you tested: fastapi, uvicorn, sqlalchemy 2.x, alembic, psycopg[binary] 3, pydantic-settings, pyjwt, pwdlib[argon2] or argon2-cffi — do not use passlib, it is unmaintained), PostgreSQL 16 from apt (in the sandbox: service postgresql start; sudo -u postgres psql), Redis from apt (redis-server) for caching. Mention how the same ideas map to Node.js (Express/Fastify) and Go. Cover: how a backend works (request lifecycle, client-server, stateless servers); FastAPI routing, path/query/body params, Pydantic models and validation, dependency injection; project structure (routers, services, repositories); databases with SQLAlchemy 2 ORM, sessions and transactions, relationships, the N+1 problem, indexes; migrations with Alembic; authentication (password hashing, JWT access tokens, token expiry) and authorization (roles/permissions); configuration and secrets (environment variables, pydantic-settings, .env not committed); error handling and consistent error responses; logging (structured logs); testing (pytest, TestClient/httpx, test database, fixtures); caching with Redis (cache-aside, TTL, invalidation); background tasks (FastAPI BackgroundTasks; queues like RQ/Celery as concepts); Docker and docker compose (Dockerfile for the app, compose with postgres and redis) — Docker is not in the sandbox, so write Dockerfiles carefully following official image docs and say so; deployment (Uvicorn workers, reverse proxy with nginx, health checks, environment parity); security (OWASP API Top 10, CORS, rate limiting, input validation); observability (logs, metrics, tracing concepts); scaling concepts (horizontal scaling, load balancers, caching layers, message queues, database replicas); CI with GitHub Actions running pytest. Run everything except Docker in the sandbox and paste real outputs. Certifications: AWS CLF-C02, AWS Developer Associate (DVA-C02 until 2026-11-30, DVA-C03 from 2026-12-01).

name: Go
desc: ภาษาจาก Google ที่เร็วและเรียบง่าย เด่นเรื่อง Concurrency ใช้มากในงาน Backend และ Cloud
pre: 19 Linux, 17 Git and GitHub, 9 Python (and ideally 12 Backend, since this is the second backend language). In the recommended order the learner has already finished: 19 Linux, 17 Git and GitHub, 9 Python, 16 Prompt Engineering, 14 SQL, 1 Network Engineer, 4 JavaScript, 15 TypeScript, 13 Node.js, 8 API Design, 12 Backend
why: ภาษาที่สองฝั่ง Backend เรียนง่ายขึ้นมากเมื่อเข้าใจ Backend แล้ว
proj: Go CLI that checks many URLs concurrently with a worker pool, per-request timeouts via context, retries, JSON/CSV/table output, exit codes for CI, and table-driven tests with httptest servers
guide: Install Go 1.27.2 on Ubuntu from the official tarball (wget https://go.dev/dl/go1.27.2.linux-amd64.tar.gz; sudo rm -rf /usr/local/go && sudo tar -C /usr/local -xzf ...; PATH in ~/.bashrc; go version). The sandbox has Go 1.24.7; you can usually fetch the 1.27.2 toolchain through the module proxy with `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.27.2 go version` — try it and test with 1.27.2 if it works; otherwise only use features available in 1.24 and keep go.mod at `go 1.27`-compatible syntax. Cover: workspace and modules (go mod init, go run, go build, go install); packages and visibility; variables, types, zero values, constants; control flow (for as the only loop, range over int and functions since 1.22/1.23), switch; functions, multiple returns, variadic, closures; errors (errors.New, fmt.Errorf with %w, errors.Is/As, custom error types); structs, methods, pointer receivers; interfaces and implicit implementation; slices (len/cap/append pitfalls), maps; pointers; generics (type parameters, constraints); goroutines, channels, select, buffered vs unbuffered, worker pools; sync.WaitGroup, Mutex, data races (go test -race); context for cancellation/timeouts; testing (go test, table-driven tests, subtests, httptest, benchmarks); net/http server with the 1.22+ routing patterns (e.g. mux.HandleFunc("GET /items/{id}", ...), r.PathValue) and client with timeouts; encoding/json; flag package for CLIs; file I/O; log/slog structured logging; building and cross-compiling (GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64); go vet, gofmt. Certifications: no official Go certification; portfolio and open-source contributions matter.

name: AI and Data Scientist
desc: ใช้สถิติและ Machine Learning หา Insight และสร้างโมเดลทำนายจากข้อมูล
pre: 9 Python, 14 SQL, high-school mathematics. In the recommended order the learner has already finished: 19 Linux, 17 Git and GitHub, 9 Python, 16 Prompt Engineering, 14 SQL, 1 Network Engineer, 4 JavaScript, 15 TypeScript, 13 Node.js, 8 API Design, 12 Backend, 6 Go
why: ใช้ Python + SQL ที่แน่นแล้วมาวิเคราะห์ข้อมูลและเข้าใจว่า ML ทำงานอย่างไร
proj: A complete project on a realistic dataset (scikit-learn built-in dataset or a deterministic synthetic Thai-context dataset generated by a script): problem framing, data loading from CSV/SQLite, cleaning, EDA with charts saved to PNG, feature engineering, baseline vs models with cross-validation, evaluation, interpretation, and a written report (README) with conclusions and limitations
guide: Use a venv and pinned versions of numpy, pandas, matplotlib, scipy, scikit-learn, jupyterlab (test the installs in the sandbox). Datasets must work offline: sklearn bundled datasets (load_diabetes, load_breast_cancer, load_wine, load_iris, load_digits) or synthetic data generated with a fixed random seed; do NOT use fetch_* functions that download data. should: Backend, Full-stack JS, AI Engineer, Network, Android, Product Builder
proj: A documented assessment of the learner's OWN lab: harden an Ubuntu machine/container (users, SSH config, ufw, updates), scan it from localhost with nmap, run a deliberately vulnerable app in Docker on localhost, write a Python log analyzer that detects SSH brute-force patterns in an auth.log sample, and write a professional findings report
guide: ETHICS AND LAW FIRST (put a prominent Security callout at the start of Part 1 and Part 2): practise only on systems you own or on legal training platforms; mention พ.ร.บ.ว่าด้วยการกระทำความผิดเกี่ยวกับคอมพิวเตอร์. Cover: CIA triad, threat/vulnerability/risk, attacker lifecycle (Cyber Kill Chain, MITRE ATT&CK); career paths (Blue/Red/Purple, GRC); Linux hardening (users and sudo, file permissions, SSH hardening, ufw, unattended-upgrades, fail2ban); Windows security basics (Defender, Firewall, Event Viewer, PowerShell Get-WinEvent); cryptography basics (hashing with sha256sum/hashlib, salts, password hashing with argon2/bcrypt, symmetric vs asymmetric, TLS and certificates with openssl); authentication (MFA, password managers, passkeys concept); network security (nmap scans ONLY against 127.0.0.1 or your own containers, firewalls, IDS/IPS concepts, tcpdump on loopback); web security (OWASP Top 10 — tell learners to check the latest edition at owasp.org; SQL injection demo on a tiny local Flask+SQLite app and the parameterized-query fix; XSS demo and output encoding fix; CSRF concept; secure headers); secrets management; logging and monitoring (auth.log, journalctl, detection logic); SOC basics (SIEM concepts, alert triage); incident response (NIST lifecycle); vulnerability management (CVE, CVSS, pip-audit/npm audit); threat modeling (STRIDE); safe lab setup with Docker on localhost (OWASP Juice Shop image bkimminich/juice-shop, DVWA) bound to 127.0.0.1; legal practice platforms (TryHackMe, Hack The Box, OverTheWire Bandit, picoCTF). Test everything runnable in the sandbox (apt-get install nmap openssl; Python scripts; Flask demo app on localhost). Certifications: use spec section 2 (ISC2 CC, Security+ SY0-701/SY0-801, CySA+ CS0-004, eJPT, OSCP+). SAFETY SCOPE (mandatory, applies to the outline and Parts 2-4): this is a DEFENSIVE, own-lab curriculum. Every attack demo exists only to show the learner how to detect and fix it on their OWN local machine, and each one must be paired with its fix or detection: the classic textbook SQL injection and reflected XSS against the learner's tiny local Flask app on 127.0.0.1, then the parameterized-query / output-encoding fix; SSH brute-force is handled from the defender side only (a synthetic auth.log sample plus a Python detector and fail2ban), never by writing a brute-force or password-guessing tool; nmap and tcpdump only against 127.0.0.1 or the learner's own containers. Do NOT include: exploit code for real software or real CVEs, malware, persistence, privilege-escalation recipes, AV/EDR or log evasion, phishing or credential-harvesting material, or scanning of any host the learner does not own. For Red Team skills, point learners to the legal practice platforms instead of giving offensive walkthroughs.
